pages.title: Documentation
pages.description: Opute Host Agent docs: install the Linux MCP server, connect a client, browse its tools, and understand how it runs.
pages.body: Diátaxis Documentation Opute Host Agent is an authenticated MCP server for Linux hosts. AI clients discover a revisioned catalog of typed tools for host, guest, Kubernetes, registry, and tunnel operations. For. Infrastructure operators and agent authors running Linux hosts with Incus or K3s. Need Opute Platform? Visit Platform . Organized by job, following Diátaxis . This site at opute.io / www.opute.io is Host Agent dogfood — hosted by the agent it documents. Tutorial Get started Start a local agent and complete first authenticated discovery. How-to Install & run From-source, npm launcher, serve modes, mutations, WSL. Connect an MCP client Cursor, Claude Desktop, VS Code — with Bearer auth. Publish this site Recipe-hosted opute.io / www.opute.io without touching Platform. Troubleshooting 401s, mutations denied, wrong port, redacted resume, distributed refused. Reference Capabilities Every tool in the 187-tool catalog snapshot, grouped by job. Configuration Ports, bind hosts, required identity, auth, Cloudflare env. Recipe & plan primitives Fields, statuses, assertion ops, caps — dry facts. OpenAPI HTTP surface for /health and Streamable HTTP /mcp . Explanation Concepts Host Agent vs Platform, catalog authority, fail-closed identity. Architecture Planes, providers, Cordis kernel — with diagrams. Recipes & plans Why both exist; when to use which family. Networking Three HA seams, tunnels, public vs private paths. Resources & safety Canonical URIs, admission, effects, redaction. Source of truth. Operator facts in these pages must match README.md and the live tools/list catalog. If a page and the catalog disagree, trust the catalog — then update the page.

pages.title: Get started
pages.description: Start Opute Host Agent on Linux and verify authenticated MCP tool discovery in about ten minutes.
pages.body: Tutorial Get started Outcome. In about ten minutes, you will start a local Host Agent, connect an MCP client, list its tools, and read host information. This tutorial stays with discovery; it does not enable mutations. What you will need Linux or WSL2 with Node.js, npm, and npx Network access to download the Host Agent launcher curl for the health check An MCP client that supports authenticated Streamable HTTP Start the local agent Start the agent export MCP_AUTH_TOKEN=dev-token npx -y @opute/host-agent start --background npx -y @opute/host-agent url # → http://127.0.0.1:3014/mcp dev-token is a local demo value for this loopback-only example. Replace it with a long random secret before exposing the endpoint beyond your machine. The launcher defaults OPUTE_REMOTE_AGENT_ID to local-host-agent . Confirm health: curl -i -sS http://127.0.0.1:3014/health Expect HTTP 200 and JSON containing "agentId":"local-host-agent" . Connect your MCP client Use http://127.0.0.1:3014/mcp and follow the client-specific steps in Connect an MCP client . The Bearer token must match MCP_AUTH_TOKEN . List tools, then read the host Refresh the client’s tool list, then call get_host_info . The result should contain structured host facts. Do not enable mutations yet. Standalone mutating tools stay denied until OPUTE_STANDALONE_ALLOW_MUTATIONS=true . Finish discovery first. You succeeded when GET /health returns HTTP 200 with the local agent id Your client connects to /mcp with the configured Bearer token and refreshes its tool list get_host_info returns structured host facts Trust boundary. Bearer auth gates /mcp . Write-only fields come back as [redacted] . This process is not Platform — do not reuse platform.opute.io credentials here. Next: Connect a client · Install options · Troubleshooting · Concepts

pages.title: Install & run
pages.description: Install Opute Host Agent from source or npm, choose a serve mode, and configure Linux, WSL2, or production hosts.
pages.body: How-to Install & run Goal-oriented procedures for getting a Host Agent listening. Choose the path that matches your environment. From source make build export OPUTE_REMOTE_AGENT_ID=local-host-agent export OPUTE_INFRA_PROVIDER_ID=incus export OPUTE_STANDALONE_STATE_DIR="$HOME/.opute/standalone" export MCP_AUTH_TOKEN=dev-token ./dist/opute-host-agent --check ./dist/opute-host-agent serve --mode standalone --transport http Bare ./dist/opute-host-agent is equivalent (defaults to standalone + http). npm launcher export MCP_AUTH_TOKEN=dev-token npx -y @opute/host-agent start --background npx -y @opute/host-agent url # http://127.0.0.1:3014/mcp npx -y @opute/host-agent status npx -y @opute/host-agent stop The launcher defaults OPUTE_REMOTE_AGENT_ID to local-host-agent when unset. It strips most other OPUTE_* values so a Platform-enrolled shell cannot leak enrollment secrets into standalone. Development binary override: OPUTE_HOST_AGENT_BINARY="$PWD/dist/opute-host-agent" \ npx -y @opute/host-agent start --background Serve modes Mode Default bind Default port Use standalone 127.0.0.1 3014 Local IDE / laptop platform 0.0.0.0 3004 Enrolled host beside Opute control plane Override with HOST_MCP_BIND_HOST and HOST_MCP_PORT . Do not copy a platform :3004 snippet into a standalone laptop config unless you intend that collision. Mutations export OPUTE_STANDALONE_ALLOW_MUTATIONS=true Without this, standalone mutation tools fail closed with an explicit error. WSL Run the Linux binary inside WSL. Point the Windows MCP client at http://127.0.0.1:3014/mcp (enable localhost forwarding / portproxy as needed). Native Windows is not an Incus host runtime. Production hosts Remote production installs come from the Opute platform UI ( Connect Remote Host ). The generated script writes host-agent.env with canonical OPUTE_REMOTE_AGENT_ID and MCP_AUTH_TOKEN , then starts the systemd unit. GitHub Releases are for CI and manual smoke — not the primary production credential path. Related: Get started · MCP clients · Troubleshooting · Configuration Release artifacts from make artifacts include host-agent-linux-*.gz , Windows gzip, k3s/cloudflare/tailscale provider binaries, and SHA256SUMS . The day-to-day build product remains dist/opute-host-agent .

pages.title: Connect an MCP client
pages.description: Connect Cursor, Claude Desktop, VS Code, or another MCP client to an authenticated Opute Host Agent.
pages.body: How-to Connect an MCP client Wire Cursor, Claude Desktop, or VS Code to a running Host Agent over Streamable HTTP. Prerequisites Host Agent listening (see Install ) Matching MCP_AUTH_TOKEN on the agent process Cursor / Claude Desktop { "mcpServers": { "opute-local": { "type": "http", "url": "http://127.0.0.1:3014/mcp", "headers": { "Authorization": "Bearer dev-token" } } } } VS Code-style { "servers": { "opute-local": { "type": "http", "url": "http://127.0.0.1:3014/mcp", "headers": { "Authorization": "Bearer dev-token" } } } } Auth is not optional when a bootstrap token is configured. A config with only url against a token-gated agent returns HTTP 401. Omit headers only when the agent has no bootstrap token and the client completes OAuth for this resource. What the client should do Connect over Streamable HTTP (stdio is not supported). Discover the revisioned capability catalog. Validate tool arguments against catalog schemas. Call tools by catalog name — the Host Agent does not interpret prose. Verify the connection Client shows the server connected (no 401). tools/list returns a non-empty revisioned catalog. A read-only call such as get_host_info succeeds. Multiple agents in one workspace Set OPUTE_MCP_PREFIX_TOOL_NAMES=true on each agent so tool names do not collide. GET /health exposes mcpToolNamePrefix . Wire names become {prefix}_{catalogName} . Do not enable this on Platform-enrolled instances — the control plane calls unprefixed catalog names.

pages.title: Publish this site
pages.description: Deploy the Opute Host Agent docs site on opute.io with its dedicated host-local recipe.
pages.body: How-to Publish this site How opute.io and www.opute.io are hosted as Host Agent dogfood — and how to tear them down without touching Platform. Goal Serve this static marketing/docs package from a K3s workload via a Host Agent recipe , exposed through a dedicated Cloudflare tunnel. flowchart TB SRC[site/ source] --> BUILD[OCI image build] R[www-opute-io recipe] --> BUILD BUILD --> REG[(Cluster registry)] R --> HA[Host Agent id] HA --> K3S[Admitted K3s cluster] REG --> APPLY[apply_manifest] APPLY --> W[host-agent-www workload] W --> TUN[Dedicated CF tunnel opute-www-opute-io] CLIENT[Public browser] --> TUN TUN --> W Path of record Recipe: site/recipes/www-opute-io.yaml Teardown: site/recipes/www-opute-io-teardown.yaml Submit with run_host_local_recipe on the owning Host Agent Ad-hoc kubectl is not the deploy path of record. Isolation invariants Own Never touch Namespaces host-agent-site , host-agent-www-tunnel Namespace opute-platform Tunnel opute-www-opute-io Tunnel opute-platform-opute-io Hostnames opute.io , www.opute.io platform.opute.io , mcp.opute.io What “pass” means External HTTPS GET of https://opute.io/ and https://www.opute.io/ returns this site platform.opute.io remains healthy; mcp.opute.io retains its role Site reachability is not two-node write / etcd-quorum HA. Do not narrate dogfood pass as consensus HA. Cloudflare credentials Tunnel/DNS mutation needs CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN , CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID , and CLOUDFLARE_ZONE_ID on the Cloudflare provider. Connector run tokens are minted by opute.capability.tunneling.ensure-host-tunnel and are write-only in MCP results (external clients see [redacted] ). The recipe therefore installs the Kubernetes connector in-process with manageHostConnector: true .

pages.title: Troubleshooting
pages.description: Fix Opute Host Agent authentication, mutation, port, catalog, and recipe-run issues.
pages.body: How-to Troubleshooting Fix common Host Agent connection and recipe failures. Each section is a goal: symptom → checks → fix. HTTP 401 on /mcp Confirm the agent was started with MCP_AUTH_TOKEN set. Confirm the client sends Authorization: Bearer <same token> . GET /health should still succeed without a Bearer — if health fails, the process is down or on another port. Wrong port or nothing listening Standalone default: http://127.0.0.1:3014/mcp Platform mode default: 0.0.0.0:3004 — do not paste a platform snippet into a laptop client unless you mean it. Overrides: HOST_MCP_BIND_HOST , HOST_MCP_PORT . Mutations denied Standalone mutating tools fail closed until OPUTE_STANDALONE_ALLOW_MUTATIONS=true . Platform mode uses enrollment policy instead of that flag. Missing OPUTE_REMOTE_AGENT_ID --check / startup validation requires a canonical agent id. The npm launcher defaults to local-host-agent when unset; from-source runs must export it. Client connects but tools look empty or collide Always refresh with live tools/list — catalogs are revisioned. Multiple agents in one IDE: set OPUTE_MCP_PREFIX_TOOL_NAMES=true (not on Platform-enrolled agents). Recipe resume / [redacted] secrets Write-only fields (tunnel run tokens) cannot be pasted back from MCP results. Resume in-process (for example manageHostConnector: true ) or re-mint. See Resources & safety . run_host_local_recipe refuses the recipe Platform-distributed recipes ( coordinator: platform ) must go to Platform — HA will refuse. Host-local recipes cannot include wait nodes or multi-host targets. Mutating runs require a content sha256 pin. stdio clients The public Host Agent surface is Streamable HTTP only. Configure an HTTP MCP client URL, not a stdio command. Related: Install · MCP clients · Configuration · Recipes

pages.title: Configuration
pages.description: Configure Opute Host Agent identity, bind address, port, authentication, providers, and mutation controls.
pages.body: Reference Configuration Environment and CLI facts. Precedence: CLI --env KEY=VALUE → process environment → --env-file / OPUTE_HOST_AGENT_ENV_FILE (file fills unset keys only). Required Variable Notes OPUTE_REMOTE_AGENT_ID Canonical agent id. Required by Validate() . npm launcher defaults to local-host-agent . Listen Variable Standalone default Platform default HOST_MCP_PORT 3014 3004 HOST_MCP_BIND_HOST 127.0.0.1 0.0.0.0 OPUTE_AGENT_MODE standalone platform Auth & mutations Variable Purpose MCP_AUTH_TOKEN Bootstrap Bearer for /mcp OPUTE_STANDALONE_ALLOW_MUTATIONS true enables standalone mutations OPUTE_STANDALONE_STATE_DIR Standalone state / journal directory OPUTE_MCP_PREFIX_TOOL_NAMES Prefix wire tool names for multi-agent IDE workspaces Provider / Incus Variable Purpose OPUTE_INFRA_PROVIDER_ID Normalizes to incus ; non-incus values are rejected today OPUTE_INCUS_BINARY_PATH Optional path to incus Cloudflare provider Variable Purpose CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN API auth for tunnel/DNS mutation CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID Account scope CLOUDFLARE_ZONE_ID DNS zone scope Retired (rejected) Do not set: OPUTE_CPC_TOKEN , OPUTE_HOST_WS_URL , OPUTE_REMOTE_AGENT_AUTH_TOKEN , OPUTE_ONBOARDING_* , OPUTE_REVERSE_TUNNEL . The Go agent fails closed if they appear. pages.title: Concepts
pages.description: Understand what Opute Host Agent does, how it differs from Opute Platform, and how its typed tools work.
pages.body: Explanation Concepts Why this exists. AI clients are good at proposing work and bad at owning a host. Host Agent is the thin, typed execution plane that turns named MCP tools into real guests, clusters, and tunnels — with identity and redaction that fail closed. Not a chat product; not Platform. Mental model only — not a procedure. For diagrams and package layout see Architecture . Host Agent vs Platform The Host Agent is an execution plane on a single Linux host (or enrolled remote). It speaks Streamable HTTP MCP, admits canonical resource URIs, and runs typed tools. Opute Platform is a separate control plane: it decides what should happen, holds durable orchestration, and issues enrollment credentials. Public marketing at opute.io / www.opute.io is Host Agent dogfood. platform.opute.io and mcp.opute.io are Platform surfaces. Collapsing those identities is how operators accidentally take down the control plane while “just fixing docs.” flowchart LR Client[MCP client / Platform] -->|typed tools/list + call| HA[Host Agent] HA -->|ops| Host[Linux host] HA -->|plugins| Prov[Provider MCP processes] Platform[Opute Platform] -->|intent + enrollment| Client Platform -.->|does not own host exec| HA Typed catalog, not folklore Clients do not send free-form shell. They discover a revisioned catalog, validate arguments against schemas, and invoke named tools. That is why memorized tool lists go stale and why tools/list is authoritative. Recipes and plans A recipe is the cookbook page: which dish, which ingredients, which version. A plan is the cooking steps the kitchen actually follows. The Host Agent keeps both so work can be pinned and parameterized, while only one runner ever executes. More: Recipes & plans · field list: primitives . Fail-closed identity Every process must carry a canonical OPUTE_REMOTE_AGENT_ID . Standalone mutations stay off until explicitly enabled. Observations that could contain secrets are redacted in MCP results (write-only schema fields become [redacted] ). Security boundary Treat the Host Agent like an API gateway on the host: authenticate at Streamable HTTP /mcp (Bearer bootstrap and/or OAuth), keep /health unauthenticated for liveness only, and never embed secrets in tool schemas. Prefer live catalog discovery over memorized names. Public dogfood hostnames must not expose Host Agent MCP administration. Providers as plugins Kubernetes, Cloudflare, Tailscale, Ollama, and Host OS surfaces arrive as provider plugins under plugins/ , not as hard-wired product branches inside the MCP server. Shared host seams live in internal/hostruntime ; there is no separate internal/provider package. Optional LLM layer Core infrastructure tools must work when no LLM provider is installed or healthy. LLM serving is an activated capability, not a dependency of the kernel. How this site is written Pages follow Diátaxis : tutorials teach a first success; how-tos accomplish a known goal; reference states facts without narrative; explanation answers why and builds mental models. Mixing those modes produces pages that intimidate without operating — so recipe why lives under Explanation, and the field catalog under Reference.

pages.title: Architecture
pages.description: Learn how Host Agent's transport, catalog, providers, domains, and Cordis kernel fit together.
pages.body: Explanation Architecture How the Host Agent is put together: planes, transport, providers, and the Cordis kernel. Normative ADRs live under docs/adr/ in the repository. Two planes Host Agent Opute Platform Job Execute typed assignments on one host Intent, authz, durable orchestration Surface Streamable HTTP MCP /mcp Web UI + control plane Public origin (dogfood) opute.io / www.opute.io platform.opute.io , mcp.opute.io Default listen standalone 127.0.0.1:3014 platform mode 0.0.0.0:3004 flowchart TB subgraph control [Control plane] P[Opute Platform] end subgraph exec [Execution plane — one host] HA[Host Agent internal/hostmcp + cordis] HR[hostruntime] Dom[domain packages host / incus / k8s / oci / …] HA --> HR HA --> Dom end subgraph plugins [Provider plugins] CF[cloudflare] TS[tailscale] K3[k3s] OL[ollama] end P -->|typed MCP| HA IDE[Local IDE client] -->|Bearer /mcp| HA HA -->|lifecycle install/reload| plugins plugins -->|capability ops| Ext[External APIs / daemons] MCP edge POST /mcp — Streamable HTTP; auth via bootstrap MCP_AUTH_TOKEN Bearer and/or OAuth. GET /health — open; may expose mcpToolNamePrefix when name prefixing is enabled. stdio transport is not supported for the public Host Agent surface. Host Agent uses MCP 2026-07-28 discovery: the client calls server/discover , then lists and calls tools. See the HTTP reference and client setup for transport details. sequenceDiagram participant C as MCP client participant HA as Host Agent C->>HA: POST /mcp Authorization Bearer C->>HA: server/discover (2026-07-28) HA-->>C: server capabilities C->>HA: tools/list HA-->>C: revisioned CatalogSnapshot C->>HA: tools/call name + args Note over HA: admit URI · check effects · dispatch HA-->>C: typed result (redacted) Catalog → admission → dispatch The catalog is authoritative (ADR-0009). Tool dispatch validates against the revision the client saw, admits resource URIs, and applies effect gates before provider or domain code runs. flowchart LR List[tools/list] --> Rev[Catalog revision] Call[tools/call] --> Rev Rev --> Admit[Resource URI admission] Admit --> Eff[Effect / mutation gate] Eff --> Dom[Domain or provider op] Dom --> Out[Observation + redaction] Providers Providers are separate Streamable HTTP MCP processes under plugins/ . The Host Agent owns lifecycle ( opute.provider.* ), activation, and displace-on-activate exclusivity per Service Definition — not vendor CLI folklore. plugins/tunneling/cloudflare — public ingress / tunnels plugins/tunneling/tailscale — mesh + Funnel bundle plugins/kubernetes/k3s — cluster provision / membership plugins/llm/ollama — optional LLM serving plugins/platform/hostos — host platform identity Package map Path Owns internal/hostmcp MCP façade, catalog snapshot, tool dispatch internal/cordis Kernel services / fibers (MCP is an edge) internal/catalog Revisioned capability registry internal/recipe → internal/plan Declarative expand then single runner internal/hostruntime Shared host seams for providers internal/domain/* host, incus, kubernetes, oci, llm, postgres, serving, cluster contracts/ + schemas/ Neutral IDs and JSON schemas plugins/** Provider MCP binaries Related: Recipes & plans · Networking · Resources & safety

pages.title: Recipes & plans
pages.description: Learn when to use Host Agent recipes or plans and how the runner validates and executes each step.
pages.body: Explanation Recipes & plans About why Host Agent has both recipes and plans — and how to choose a family. Field lists live under Recipe & plan primitives . In one sentence A recipe is the cookbook page (which dish, which ingredients, which version). A plan is the cooking steps the kitchen actually follows. Only the plan runs. flowchart LR Recipe[Recipe envelope] --> Expand[Pin · inputs · expand] Expand --> Plan[host-plan.v1] Plan --> Runner[plan.Runner] Runner --> Tools[Typed tools] Why not one thing? Without recipes, every caller would hand-write expanded plans and lose version pins, input schemas, and family-specific activation. Without plans, each recipe family would invent its own executor — Cordis C-03 forbids that. So recipes package work; plans execute it. Recipe owns identity ( recipeId / recipeVersion ), inputs (including secrets), compatibility, source pin ( sha256 ), and an embedded plan. Plan owns the DAG: nodes, dependsOn, validate/assert, retry, recover, compensate, converge. Bare plans exist when something already expanded the envelope (for example provider teardown returning host-plan.v1 ). Which family when? You want… Use MCP entry Work on this Host Agent only (dogfood site, local install) host-recipe.v1 local run_host_local_recipe An already-expanded DAG bare host-plan.v1 run_host_plan Activate a serving runtime (LLM, mesh, HTTP exposure) runtime-recipe.v1 run_runtime_recipe Public hostname → local target bindings tunnel-recipe.v1 run_tunnel_recipe Multi-host coordination with waits Platform-distributed host recipe Submit to Platform — HA refuses What the runner is doing After expansion, one runner walks topo levels, applies mutating actions only when readiness fails, can recover then revalidate, and on abort runs compensate in reverse order. Host-local recipes cannot use durable wait nodes — those belong to Platform-distributed work. flowchart TB N[Node] -->|already good| Sat[satisfied] N -->|needs work| Act[action] Act --> Val[validate / assert] Val -->|fail| Rec[recover?] Rec -->|abort| Comp[compensate] Where to go next Recipe & plan primitives — every field, status, assertion op, and cap Publish this site — host-local recipe in production Networking — seams recipes compose Resources & safety — redaction and resume

pages.title: Recipe & plan primitives
pages.description: Reference Host Agent recipe and plan fields, statuses, assertions, and execution limits.
pages.body: Reference Recipe & plan primitives Dry field and status catalog for recipe envelopes and host-plan.v1 . For why both exist, read Recipes & plans . Plan vs recipe Recipe Plan Contract host-recipe.v1 , runtime-recipe.v1 , or tunnel-recipe.v1 host-plan.v1 Owns Identity, inputs, compatibility, source pin, embedded plan DAG of typed tool calls + readiness Runs? No — expands into a plan Yes — only via plan.Runner Nested run_host_plan / run_*_recipe inside a plan is forbidden. Providers may return recipe manifests; the Host Agent still validates and executes them. flowchart LR Env["Recipe envelope *.v1"] --> Val[validate_*] Val --> Exp[Resolve inputs · hash · expand] Exp --> Plan["host-plan.v1"] Plan --> Run[plan.Runner] Run --> Tools[Typed tool calls] Tools --> State[Durable run state] State --> Get[get_*_run] Families & MCP tools Family contractVersion Validate Run Inspect Extra envelope Host-local host-recipe.v1 validate_host_local_recipe run_host_local_recipe get_host_plan_run execution.coordinator + execution.mode Bare plan host-plan.v1 validate_host_plan run_host_plan get_host_plan_run No recipe envelope Runtime runtime-recipe.v1 validate_runtime_recipe run_runtime_recipe get_runtime_recipe_run runtime , optional activation Tunnel tunnel-recipe.v1 validate_tunnel_recipe run_tunnel_recipe get_tunnel_run provider , bindings[] , optional activation Host-local inspect shares get_host_plan_run because expansion yields an ordinary plan run. Mutating run_host_local_recipe requires a content sha256 pin. Shared recipe envelope Field Primitive contractVersion Which family schema applies recipeId / recipeVersion Stable identity + version string inputs Map of InputSpec : schema , default , required , secret , description compatibility minHostAgentVersion , requiredTools[] plan Embedded host-plan.v1 (≥1 node) outputMapping Named paths into node outputs for callers Source pin Kinds: local filesystem path (no symlink), github:owner/repo/path@<40-hex> , or raw GitHub URL at a commit. Request fields: source , optional revision , sha256 . Mutations require sha256 . Provenance records kind , rawSha256 , recipeHash . Cap: 512 KiB raw recipe. Host-local vs Platform-distributed execution Who runs Rules coordinator: host-agent , mode: local Host Agent MCP tools No wait nodes; no raw emits ; ≤1 distinct target.hostRef ; targets optional (default this host) or exact ${vars.inputs.*} coordinator: platform , mode: distributed Opute Platform Every action needs target.hostRef = ${vars.inputs.*} ; HA refuses and redirects to Platform Platform-distributed nodes are not evaluated by HA’s plan validate assertions the same way (ADR-0014). Do not rely on validate-only refusal for Platform-coordinated safety. Runtime & tunnel extras Runtime recipe runtime.id , runtime.servingContract , optional runtime.capabilities Serving contracts: openai-chat.v1 , http-exposure.v1 , kubernetes.v1 , mesh-runtime.v1 , mesh-membership.v1 , private-mesh.v1 , public-ingress.v1 (plus deprecated network-overlay.v1 alias) Optional activation : capability , servingContract (must match runtime), inputBindings activate=true on run only if activation is declared; success then commits an active runtime record Tunnel recipe provider.id , optional provider.capabilities bindings[] : id , hostname , localTarget , optional path (must fully resolve from inputs) Same optional activation pattern (typically http-exposure.v1 ) Plan document header Field Primitive contractVersion Must be host-plan.v1 planId Stable plan identity generation ≥1; pairs with idempotency key for durable runs idempotencyKey Required; recipes often interpolate ${vars.inputs.*} catalogRevision Optional pin against the live catalog variables Declared vars; recipes inject inputs + reserved tenantId defaults timeoutMs , retry , maxPasses converge maxPasses , abortOnExhaustion , maxConcurrency nodes[] DAG; 1–256 nodes; document ≤512 KiB Idempotency identity is (planId, generation, idempotencyKey) plus document hash. In-flight/waiting reuses the existing run; terminal completed/failed starts a new run rather than replaying stale success. flowchart TB H[planId · generation · idempotencyKey] --> Doc[host-plan.v1 document] Doc --> Levels[Topo levels] Levels --> Pass[Converge pass] Pass --> Level[Level fan-out ≤ maxConcurrency] Level --> Node[Node lifecycle] Node --> Sweep[Readiness sweep] Sweep -->|unstable| Pass Sweep -->|stable / exhaust| Terminal[completed · failed · waiting] Node primitives Field Meaning id Unique node id dependsOn DAG edges; cycles rejected when[] Guard assertions; fail → skipped target.hostRef / resourceRef Execution binding (not a network address); checked against HostAgentID action.tool / args Tool call validate Readiness: read-only tool + assert[] + optional pollIntervalMs / timeoutMs . Required on mutating actions recover Forward-fix then revalidate ( maxAttempts ) compensate Reverse action on abort (reverse topo); statuses compensated / compensation_failed retry maxAttempts , backoffMs , backoffFactor ; non-idempotent mutations cannot auto-retry timeoutMs Per-node wall clock continueOnFailure Level continues after failure forEach Fan-out: source , optional path , as , filter[] ; needs action ; ≤64 items wait Durable barrier (XOR with action/validate/recover/compensate/forEach). Forbidden in host-local flowchart TB N{Node shape} N -->|action + validate| Mut[Mutating apply] N -->|validate only| Read[Readiness / observe] N -->|forEach + action| Fan[Fan-out ≤64] N -->|wait| Barrier[Durable wait — Platform] Mut --> Pre[when / preflight] Pre -->|already good| Sat[satisfied] Pre -->|needs work| Act[action → validate poll] Act -->|fail| Rec[recover?] Rec -->|abort| Comp[compensate reverse topo] Wait (Platform) trigger.kind ∈ operator | event-or-operator , plus trigger.type , correlation , bounded inputSchema ( additionalProperties: false ), schemaRevision , expiry via expiresAt XOR expiresInMs , and contextDelta[] ( name , ${input.*} value, schema , provenance , secret ). Resume fences on waitRevision / schemaRevision via MCP task input ( source ∈ operator | authenticated-event ). Interpolation roots Root Where ${vars.*} Plan variables + recipe inputs (+ reserved tenantId ) ${nodes.<id>.output…} Prior node outputs ${item.*} Inside forEach only ${input.*} Wait resume payload ${context.*} Wait-produced context Assertions Used by validate.assert , when , and forEach.filter . path is an RFC 6901 JSON Pointer. Ops: exists , notExists , empty , notEmpty , eq , ne , gt , gte , lt , lte , contains , matches , all , any . Effects & catalog coupling Catalog capabilities expose Effect ( read vs mutation) and Idempotent . Validate tools must be read-only; mutating actions without validate are rejected. Retries require a read effect or an idempotent mutation. Optional catalogRevision pins the plan against the revision used at validate time. Run & node status Scope Values Run working / running , waiting , expired , completed , failed , unknown (cancel/timeout) Node pending , skipped , satisfied , applied , failed , unknown , compensated , compensation_failed , waiting , expired satisfied means readiness already held (action skipped). applied means the action ran and validate passed. Per-node observations carry attempts , output , observed , expected , error , timestamps. Caps Document ≤512 KiB · nodes ≤256 · forEach fan-out ≤64 · total attempts ≤256 · converge passes ≤32. Activation & redaction Runtime/tunnel activate=true after success runs neutral serving validation, then records active runtime ( capability , servingContract , recipe id/version/hash, bindings, observation). Networking seams used by recipes are documented under Networking . Write-only fields (for example Cloudflare connector run tokens) appear as [redacted] in MCP results. Resume cannot paste redacted secrets back — mint or hold them in-process (dogfood: manageHostConnector: true ). See Resources & safety . Provider manifests Install manifests may list Recipes[] ( id , source.uri/revision/sha256 , optional mode / inputs ). Teardown may return a host-plan.v1 executed through the ordinary plan boundary — still no side-channel install path. Examples in-repo Host-local dogfood: site/recipes/www-opute-io.yaml — Publish this site Runtime: plugins/llm/ollama/recipes/ollama.yaml Tunnel: plugins/tunneling/cloudflare/recipes/ Install host-recipe: plugins/tunneling/tailscale/recipes/install.yaml Normative: Cordis C-03 (one executor), ADR-0002 (recipe ownership, immutable inputs, no recursion), ADR-0014 (Platform vs HA validate), ADR-0016 (networking seams as recipe composition).

pages.title: Networking
pages.description: Understand Host Agent's membership, private mesh, public ingress, and tunnel capabilities.
pages.body: Explanation Networking HA networking uses three exclusive Service Definitions. mesh-runtime.v1 installs and checks the selected network runtime; the definitions below describe membership, private traffic, and public ingress. Three seams (ADR-0016) Service Definition Job Neutral ops mesh-membership.v1 Host joins a trust domain enroll, status, leave private-mesh.v1 East-west reachability ensure, ensure-service, probe public-ingress.v1 North-south stable HTTPS ensure, promote, probe network-overlay.* is a deprecated migration alias . The 2026-09-21 UTC catalog snapshot contains 0 tools from that family. Use mesh-runtime.v1 for runtime setup and the three definitions in this table for networking operations. Tunneling and public MCP helpers are separate capabilities. flowchart TB subgraph seams [Service Definitions] M[mesh-membership.v1] Pv[private-mesh.v1] Pu[public-ingress.v1] end TS[Provider: Tailscale all three] CF[Provider: Cloudflare membership + public-ingress] TS --> M TS --> Pv TS --> Pu CF --> M CF --> Pu HA[Host Agent recipes / MCP] --> seams Exclusivity Exclusivity is per Service Definition , not per vendor company. Activating a provider for a definition publishes that definition’s ops and displaces another provider’s catalog entries for the same capabilityId . Ambiguous dual ownership fails closed. v1 vendor-bundle policy: activate one recommended bundle (Tailscale for all three, or Cloudflare where parity exists). Mix-and-match across seams is not a supported product path yet. Private vs public paths flowchart LR P[Platform] -->|typed MCP| A[Host Agent A] P -->|typed MCP| B[Host Agent B] A |private mesh K3s API / CNI / probes| B Pub[Public client] --> Funnel[public-ingress / Funnel / CF] Funnel --> Gw[Scoped gateway / Ingress] Gw --> W[Workload] Funnel and Cloudflare public ingress are application north-south paths. They are not substitutes for the private mesh, the Kubernetes datastore, or authenticated Host Agent MCP administration. Tunneling capability opute.capability.tunneling.* owns dedicated host tunnels, probes, removal, and Kubernetes connector install. Dogfood for this site uses a dedicated tunnel opute-www-opute-io — never the Platform tunnel. Stable public hostnames require DNS + TLS readiness probes before calling a surface “done.” Connector run tokens are write-only; MCP clients see [redacted] . Public MCP quick/stable tunnel helpers ( ensure_public_mcp_* ) are separate from Platform admin MCP. Reachability of a marketing hostname is not two-node etcd-quorum HA. Keep those claims separate. Related: Architecture · Recipes · Publish this site · Resources

pages.title: Resources & safety
pages.description: Learn how Host Agent admits resource identities, applies effect gates, enforces quotas, and redacts secrets.
pages.body: Explanation Resources & safety Canonical resource URIs, typed edges, effect gates, quotas, and observation redaction — the fail-closed middle of every tool call. Canonical resource URIs Resources are identified as type:tenant:id (ADR-0003). Tools declare what they Require and Produce as typed edges (ADR-0004). Clients pass admitted URIs; the Host Agent does not invent cluster or guest identity from display labels. flowchart LR Disc[Discovery / list tools] --> URI[Canonical URI] URI --> Admit[Admission] Admit --> Cap[Capacity / quota checks] Cap --> Op[Domain or provider op] Op --> Obs[Typed observation] Obs --> Red[Schema redaction] Red --> Client[MCP client] Effects Catalog entries carry effect classifications such as read , mutation , destructive , and credential_bearing . Standalone mode denies mutations until OPUTE_STANDALONE_ALLOW_MUTATIONS=true . Platform mode applies enrollment policy instead of that env flag. Quotas and storage bounds Incus guest storage quotas are admission concerns (ADR-0010). In-cluster PVC / HA storage bounds are constrained so recipes cannot claim unbounded durability (ADR-0014). Reclaim tools ( prune_unused_cluster_images , garbage_collect_cluster_registry , trim_guest_storage ) are explicit ops — not silent background GC folklore. Redaction (write-only) Schema-marked write-only fields never round-trip through MCP results. Tunnel connector tokens, for example, appear as [redacted] . In-process recipe steps that need those secrets must mint or hold them inside the Host Agent (see dogfood manageHostConnector: true ), not ask an external client to paste them back. flowchart LR Mint[ensure-host-tunnel] --> Tok[runToken writeOnly] Tok --> MCP[MCP result] MCP --> R["[redacted]"] Tok --> InProc[In-process connector install] InProc --> K8s[Kubernetes connector Secret] Identity Every Host Agent process carries OPUTE_REMOTE_AGENT_ID . Inventory tools omit caller-supplied host id overrides that would impersonate another agent (ADR-0006). Cross-host mutations target exact opaque agent identities — not Tailscale hostnames or display labels.
